info.bio:
Formada en 1989 en Manchester, Reino Unido, The Charlatans UK es una de las bandas típicas de la denominada corriente Madchester junto a los Stone Roses y los Happy Mondays. Desde sus inicios, la banda formada por Rob Collins en teclados, Jon Baker en Guitarra - luego reemplazado por Mark Collins, Martin Blunt en bajo y Jon Brooks en batería probó varios vocalistas hasta dar con Tim Burgess, quien fuera el cantante definitivo de la banda.

En 1990

scenes.name: San Francisco: Acid Tests y Haight-Ashbury
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: A principios de 1966 había distritos psicodélicos con locales, grupos, ropa, impresos y drogas propios en Londres, Los Ángeles y San Francisco. Los Merry Pranksters de Ken Kesey convirtieron su desafío «Can You Pass the Acid Test?» en fiestas de luces, cine y sonido grabado y devuelto al instante: la segunda, en San José en diciembre de 1965 tras un concierto de los Stones, y nueve más en los tres primeros meses de 1966 (cinco en Los Ángeles, una en Watts). Los beats se habían mudado de North Beach a Haight-Ashbury; los Thelin abrieron la Psychedelic Shop y con Stewart Brand se hizo el Trips Festival (6.000 personas). La banda sonora era Rubber Soul. El caos sustituía al cuidado de Leary por el «set and setting»: en el Acid Test de Watts, Ken Babbs amplificó por micrófono los gritos de una chica en pleno mal viaje.

scenes.name: Madchester y ambient house
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Un movimiento de Manchester que marca la música de baile como ningún otro de los ochenta: la fusión de psicodelia, techno y pop. KLF importa el acid house; los Stone Roses mezclan ritmos disco hipnóticos, melodías pegadizas y entusiasmo sesentero; los Happy Mondays de Shaun Ryder (Bummed) y Black Grape; Charlatans, Nitzer Ebb, Shamen, Pop Will Eat Itself, Jesus Jones. Más allá de la moda, 808 State (herederos de Kraftwerk, «Pacific State»), William Orbit, Richard Kirk, A Guy Called Gerald, el collage de Coldcut y Primal Scream (Screamadelica).

Apart from the Charlatans, who were heavily styled in nineteenth-century Wild West costumes that reflected the city’s outlaw history, none of the musicians looked mod.…

podcast.title: Rob Collins Armed Robbery Conviction (1992–1993) – Friend Robbed Liquor Store "To Impress His Rock Star Friend"
podcast.body: On December 3, 1992, keyboardist Rob Collins drove an old school friend named Michael Whitehouse to a liquor store and waited in the car. Michael robbed the store — reportedly to impress his rock star friend — and ran back to the car; Collins drove away without knowing the full extent of what had just happened. Witnesses got his license plate number. Three hours later, police arrested Collins; he spent five days in custody while Whitehouse confessed to armed robbery. Original charges of armed robbery and possession of a firearm were reduced to assisting an offender after the crime. At trial on September 21, 1993, Whitehouse was sentenced to four years; Collins received eight months and served time as prisoner RD1533 at Redditch Open Prison, where a fellow inmate hummed the melody of a Charlatans song at him in the showers. Collins died in a car crash on July 22, 1996. "His buddy Michael confessed to armed robbery and then Rob began to talk."

podcast.title: Declared Influence
podcast.body: The Charlatans are among a partial list of artists and bands who have publicly stated that they have been influenced by Joy Division in some way. "You too, arcade fire, smashing pumpkins, nine inch nails, to pesh mode, sisters of mercy, ministry, chain addiction, the smiths, Bjork, Jesus and Marychain, Moby, primal scream, the Charlotains, Interpol, editors, white lies, Frans Ferdinand. I could go on, but I think you get the point."

podcast.title: Early Recognition
podcast.body: The speaker recalled reading about The Charlatans and immediately recognizing their potential to become a significant band. The radio station's staff enthusiastically supported their music, believing they were leading the culture in Toronto, Ontario, Western New York, and possibly beyond, particularly for British music. "I remember reading about the Happy Mondays and thinking, okay, this band is going to be something along with the stone roses and the charlatans."

podcast.body: Gazz Wheeling recalls Noel Gallagher having a falling out with Shaun Ryder but maintaining a good relationship with Clint Boon, The Charlatans' keyboard player, through whom Gazz and his wife Kelly knew Noel. xref.title: Influential British Band
xref.body: Emerging from Britain in the late 1980s, The Stone Roses became one of the most popular and influential bands of their time. By 1988, they had developed a new sound that blended 60s pop, 60s psychedelia, and modern dance, perfectly fitting the era of rave and house music in the UK, especially with the popularity of ecstasy. "Out of all the bands to come out of Britain in the late 1980s, no one was more popular and influential than the Stone Roses."

xref.body: Rob Collins of The Charlatans UK was noted for playing an actual Hammond B3 organ in the early 1990s. This usage marked a resurgence of the B3 sound, which had previously been considered outdated during the punk era. "Here's Rob Collins with the Charlotteson UK playing an actual B3."
